newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: High wages keep Australia jobless high - Costello.
newsitem.headline: High wages keep Australia jobless high - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that high wage claims in a low inflation environment were a recipe for keeping unemployment high.

Costello told the National Press Club that while Australia had a consumer price index (CPI) rate around one percent, and an underlying inflation rate around two percent, wages claims of five and eight percent were still being pursued.
"On a two percent inflation rate, an eight percent wages claim is a recipe for unemployment," Costello said.
"It's not a wage claim to keep up the cost of living," Costello said.

In the budget delivered on Tuesday, wages growth in the 1997/98 (July/June) year was forecast at four percent, while the unemployment rate was expected to be at eight percent in the June quarter of 1998.
Consumer price inflation was forecast at one percent through 1997/98, while underlying inflation was forecast at two percent.

"You'd have to say it would be a very funny employment situation where with eight percent unemployment and inflation at two percent, you're getting wages claims for eight percent, which could only worsen a bad employment situation," Costello said.
